scope: Client-side authentication flow: session management, API interceptor, login handler, and dashboard initialization

evidence.observation: Access token is stored in module-scoped variable that is initialized to null and only in-memory (not persisted to localStorage, sessionStorage, or cookies)
Access token is set only in memory; no persistence mechanism
Logout clears token and redirects to /login; fetch error is silently caught
Refresh token endpoint uses credentials: include (sends refresh token via cookie), returns false on any non-ok status without error visibility
API interceptor handles 401 by attempting refresh; throws error on failed refresh but no catch handler in dashboard useEffect
Dashboard useEffect calls 3 parallel API requests with Promise.all but has no .catch() handler for errors
Login sets token in memory then navigates to /; token is lost on page refresh before reaching Dashboard
API client checks memory-only token at function call time; if page was refreshed and app re-initialized, token is null

hypotheses.statement: User lands on Dashboard after login, then refreshes the page. On refresh, the module-scoped _accessToken variable is reset to null (C1), so subsequent API calls in Dashboard useEffect are made without Authorization header (C8), causing 401 responses that trigger the refresh flow.

Dashboard useEffect has no .catch() handler (C6), so when api() calls throw 'Session expired' after failed refresh, the error is an unhandled rejection and the user just sees the login redirect (from logout()) with no UI error.
The 3 concurrent api() calls in Promise.all each independently call refreshSession() on 401, resulting in 3 simultaneous POST /auth/refresh requests with the same refresh token cookie.
The silent redirect to login is caused by logout() being invoked inside api() when refreshSession() returns false — no error UI is ever shown to the user.
refreshSession() is not deduplicated or guarded; it is a raw function invoked independently by each concurrent api() call, so all three fire POST /auth/refresh in parallel.
